_comment: Central tweakables for a run. max_posting_age_days: drop postings older than this many days (by their posted date); set to 0 or null to keep all ages. Postings with an unknown date are always kept. fit_scoring_enabled: master off-switch for the Anthropic API — set false to skip all LLM fit scoring (e.g. test runs), regardless of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. star_within_days: mark postings newer than this many days with a star in the report; 0/null disables the star. allow_international_remote: when false (default), remote roles whose location names a non-US country (e.g. 'United Kingdom - Remote') are dropped; set true to keep all remote roles regardless of country. remote_search.enabled: master switch for the US-remote lane (reads remote_companies.json, runs profiles with remote_search:true against a US-remote gate). staffing_search.enabled: master switch for the contract/staffing lane (reads staffing_companies.json, runs profiles with staffing_search:true against the local+US-remote gate; the fetchers surface contract-type roles only). staffing_search.max_age_days: optional per-lane age window for the contract lane, overriding max_posting_age_days (falls back to it when unset).
_email_comment: email.enabled: run-wide master switch for SENDING the reports. Per-person delivery lives in profiles.json as `email` (default true); this is the master switch on top of it, so setting this false silences everyone at once. It is DELIVERY ONLY — every profile still fetches, diffs, writes its snapshot and lifecycle DB, and writes report_<name>.md/.html into the repo. That is deliberately different from `enabled:false` on a profile, which stops the work: a profile that stops running freezes its snapshot, so the first run after switching it back on diffs against a stale snapshot and arrives as one enormous months-long backlog email. Pause with `email`, not with `enabled`, unless you want the work stopped too. CURRENT STATE: Chad is paused (profiles.json email:false); Lisa is on.
_toggles_comment: Three switches are PER PROFILE, in profiles.json, not here: `email` (default true) pauses one person's DELIVERY without pausing their search; `fit_scoring` (default true) turns LLM ranking off for one person without disabling their report — scoring is the whole Anthropic bill, so a profile nobody is actively job-hunting on should not pay it; and `sheet_export` (default FALSE, opt-in) decides whose records reach the shared Google Sheet, because that sheet is one person's working document. The keys below are the run-wide master switches on top of those: fit_scoring_enabled false stops ALL scoring, sheets.enabled false stops ALL export, email.enabled false stops ALL sending.
_priority_comment: priority_search.enabled: master switch for the PRIORITY-EMPLOYER lane (reads priority_companies.json, runs profiles with priority_search:true). Its geography is location_priority below, not the Utah-only local gate, and its rows are stamped so the discovery gate retrieves them on one signal instead of two (see classify_match). Optional priority_search.max_age_days gives the lane its own window; priority_search.regions overrides location_priority for the gate alone. location_priority: the reader's location / work-arrangement preference, BEST FIRST. It is one setting doing two jobs so the order can never disagree with itself — it is the priority lane's geography AND the tiebreak the change digest ranks on within a fit score. It is a tiebreak, never a filter: a strong Utah-hybrid role still outranks a weak US-remote one. Valid names are the keys of REGION_GATES in jobmonitor.py: remote_us, utah, washington.
_v3_comment: V3 keys. lifecycle.exceptional_score: a role older than 14 days is only repeated in the digest if it scores at least this AND was independently verified still open on the same run — the two conditions together are what stop stale roles recurring forever. lifecycle.verify_limit: how many such roles may be URL-checked per run (each costs one request, so this is a hard budget, not a target). lifecycle.prune_after_days: how long a closed record is kept before being dropped — records carrying a human decision are kept regardless. discovery.max_new_scored_per_run: ceiling on NEW roles sent to Claude in one run; broad discovery multiplies new roles per day and the bill is proportional to exactly that. Roles over the cap are kept and scored on the next run, never dropped. sheets.enabled: write discovery_log_<profile>.csv and, when SHEETS_WEBHOOK_URL is set, push to the Prospector Discovery Log tab.
